transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

I... well, I'm here because of some things I've been hearing. It's... it's my partner, Garrett. I keep hearing his voice. Like, clear as day. Sometimes when I'm out on the trail, or... or in my painting room. It sounds like he's standing right behind me. I mean, I know he's dead, but... when it happens, it just feels so real.
Do you ever hear other voices or sounds that aren't there, or is it only Garrett’s voice that you hear?
No. It's... just him. I haven't heard anyone else.
Have you ever seen things that others don't see, or noticed anything unusual in your vision when Garrett's voice is present?

No. I don't see anything. It's... like I said, it's just the voice. I just keep hearing him, as clearly as if he's standing right behind me. On the trail, or... in the painting room. 

I know he's dead. I do. But... in the moment it happens, it just feels completely real. That's all. Just the voice.
Can you describe what happens just before you hear Garrett’s voice? Is there anything specific that seems to trigger it, like thinking about him or being in a certain place?

I don't know. I haven't really... paid attention to what happens right before. It just happens. 

I guess I'm usually just... doing things. Walking. Painting. I don't think I'm doing anything special to make it happen. It just comes.
Do you notice that Garrett's voice tends to come up more often when you're feeling particularly down, hopeless, or depressed—or maybe when you're feeling unusually energized or on edge?

I suppose... it was more when I was wired. That stretch where I barely slept. I was just taking on all these impossible projects, feeling like I had to just... keep going. 

I never heard him before that. It wasn't... it didn't happen during ordinary grief. It only started when things shifted like that.

When you hear Garrett's voice, are you absolutely sure there's no actual external sound or source causing it—like a recording, someone speaking nearby, or even the wind? And does it happen only during times when you're feeling especially manic or down, or can it also happen when you're feeling more stable?

I... I'm sure it's not a recording. Or the wind. Like I said before, it's... it's just his voice. As clear as if he's right there behind me. 

And... I don't know about when I'm stable. I haven't been... I haven't really felt normal in a while. But part of me knows he's gone. It's just... when I hear it, it's real. That's all.
When you hear Garrett’s voice, does it usually say specific things—like commenting on what you’re doing, giving you commands, or talking to you directly?

He just... talks to me directly. Like I said, it's... it's just like he's standing right behind me. If I'm out on the trail, or... or in my painting room. 

I know he's dead. I know that. But... when he speaks, it's just him. It's real. I don't really want to get into exactly what he says. It's just... his voice.
Can you remember if Garrett’s voice ever came up when you were feeling more stable, or does it only happen during times when you’re feeling especially manic or down?

I... I thought I mentioned this a minute ago. It really only started during that stretch when I was wired. When I wasn't sleeping, just... taking on all those projects and feeling like I couldn't stop. 

Before things shifted like that... I never heard him. Even during just normal grief, it didn't happen. So, no. Not when things were stable.

Have you ever experienced any other unusual sensations, like feeling like someone is watching you, or hearing other sounds or voices that aren’t there—especially during those times when you felt especially manic or down?

No. I... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. 

I'm only here because... well, like I said, it's just Garrett's voice. That's the only thing. Just him, as clear as if he's standing right behind me on the trail or in my painting room. Even though I know he's dead... in the moment, it just feels completely real. That's all it is. No other voices or... whatever else you said. Just him.
When you hear Garrett's voice, does it ever talk about you when you're not directly interacting with it, like commenting on your actions or thoughts, or is it always speaking directly to you?

I thought I just answered this... It's just him talking to me. Directly. Like I said, it's just like he's standing right behind me on the trail, or in my painting room. 

He doesn't... narrate what I'm doing or anything like that. It's just his voice. Even though part of me knows he's dead, when it happens, it just... it feels completely real. That's really all I can say about it.
Does Garrett’s voice only occur during times when you feel especially manic, or has it ever happened at other times, even when you felt more like yourself?

I... I thought we just went over this. 

Like I said before... it only started when I was... wired. When I wasn't sleeping and just kept taking on all those projects. I never heard him before that started. Not even when I was just... grieving normally. Only when I was like that.
Has Garrett’s voice ever occurred outside of those manic periods, or has it only happened when you were feeling especially wired and not sleeping?

I... yeah. I mean, I just said that. 

It was only during that stretch. When I was... wired. Barely sleeping, taking on all those impossible projects, just driven to keep going. I never heard him before that started. Not when I was just... grieving. Only then.
Has Garrett's voice ever said anything that made you feel afraid, confused, or instructed you to do something, or has it only ever spoken to you in a normal, conversational way?

No. Nothing like that. 

He doesn't... give me orders or try to scare me. It's just normal. Just... him talking to me. That's all.

During those times when you felt especially wired and weren't sleeping much, did you also notice any other changes in your mood or thinking, like feeling unusually confident, having thoughts race through your head, or feeling like you had extra energy or needed to keep working on projects all the time?

I mean... yeah. I guess I had a lot of energy. 

I would just stay up... writing these whole outlines for new treatment programs. Emailing colleagues, offering to mentor extra people. And... starting a bunch of canvases all at once. I just couldn't stop working on things, even though... looking back, none of it was really realistic.
